clue.text: A little whisky late on is so gorgeous

parts.note: a drop is a small measure of a drink such as whisky
dead, as in 'the late king', means late

explanation.surface: A nightcap taken late in the evening makes everything look wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop-dead gorgeous' is the stock phrase, so the answer works as an intensifying adjective meaning stunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop-dead describes someone stunningly attractive, the same idea as gorgeous in informal speech.

clue.text: Stop son being taken in by religious believer

indicators.note: the son is taken into the believer, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a deist believes in God on the evidence of reason

explanation.surface: A parent begs a son to stop being swayed by a zealous convert.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or leave off doing something, a verb synonym of stop.

clue.text: Almost insult one composer and another

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to offend someone is to insult them
another composer, J S Bach

explanation.surface: One composer nearly offends both himself and a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from OFFEND; 'another' leans on 'composer' to supply a second one, Bach.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach wrote operettas such as Orpheus in the Underworld, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Stop working girl acquiring fur

indicators.note: the girl takes on the fur after her, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
sable is a prized fur from a marten

explanation.surface: A girl stops going to work once she gets a fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To disable a machine is to make it stop working, a causative sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Policeman may ask you to move this

definitions.text: Policeman may ask you to move this

parts.words: Policeman may ask you to move this
parts.note: a policeman says 'move ...!', so the word that completes his order is the one wanted

explanation.definitionFit: Constables tell loiterers to 'move along', so the adverb is what they are asked to move, playfully.

clue.text: Staff direction from two levels inhibiting secretary

indicators.note: the levels hold back, enclose, the secretary between them

parts.note: A level and O level are the British school exams, giving A and O
a temp is a temporary secretary

explanation.surface: A temporary secretary is held back by two grades of exam and told what to do by staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A and O are A-levels and O-levels, British school exam grades. 'Staff' is the musical stave, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempo is a musical marking telling players to return to the original speed, a direction written on the stave.

clue.text: Real ridicule that's got under the skin

parts.note: true means real or genuine
to rib someone is to tease or ridicule them

explanation.surface: Genuine mockery that really gets to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got under the skin' looks like 'annoyed', but it is literal: a rib lies beneath the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A true rib is one joined directly to the breastbone, a bone lying beneath the skin of the chest.

clue.text: No official dress for legal expert

definitions.meaning: plain clothes worn by someone who normally wears uniform
a Muslim scholar who gives rulings on Islamic law

explanation.definitionFit: Mufti means civilian clothes worn off duty, and is also the title of an Islamic jurist.

clue.text: Likely to disappoint? New ball isn't

definitions.meaning: something hyped beyond its merits is bound to let people down
in cricket a ball that is no longer new has done its overs

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer as OVER'S OLD: a cricket over of six deliveries; a ball that is not new has been bowled through old overs.
explanation.definitionFit: A product oversold has been praised beyond its worth, so it is likely to disappoint buyers.

clue.text: Court trouble, because involved in a bit of satire

indicators.note: the word for because is wrapped inside the satirical piece

parts.note: a skit is a short satirical sketch, here with the article A
for can mean because, as in 'for he was tired'

explanation.surface: A comic sketch lands its writer in court because of its satire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is the verb, to invite, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for it is to invite trouble by your own behaviour, an idiom matching court trouble.

clue.text: What she foots, perhaps?

parts.note: shuffling the letters of the words soft shoe gives exactly these two words

explanation.surface: A woman dances, tapping her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: A dance she might foot, and also a hint: shuffle the letters of SOFT SHOE and you get SHE FOOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Footing it means dancing, and the soft-shoe shuffle is a tap-style dance done in soft-soled shoes.

clue.text: Drop round with book, a heavy weight

indicators.note: the word for drop goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop
and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone lets fall a heavy load along with a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandbag is a sack filled with sand, used as a heavy weight or ballast.

clue.text: The age of family responsibilities?

parts.note: the decade suited to family ties

explanation.definitionFit: The decade of one's life from forty to forty-nine, often when people are bound by family commitments.

clue.text: In bank, a very purple plant

indicators.note: the article and abbreviation sit inside the word for bank

parts.note: a bank is a lender of money

explanation.surface: A bank of purple flowers by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a riverbank of flowers, but it is the financial kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant shrub with pale purple flowers, an example of a purple-flowered plant.

clue.text: When life in Europe was not fair?

definitions.text: When life in Europe was not fair?

parts.words: When life in Europe was not fair?
parts.note: fair means light rather than just: an era that was not light

explanation.definitionFit: The early medieval period in Europe, traditionally viewed as lacking learning, a time without enlightenment.

clue.text: All talking at once with Childline?

parts.note: the one word splits into child and line: a babe is a young child, and L abbreviates line

explanation.surface: A children's helpline is swamped with callers speaking together.
explanation.walkthrough: Childline is a British telephone helpline for children; the word splits into CHILD and LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A babel is a confused noise of many voices, from the Tower of Babel story.

clue.text: Almost stomachs touring island wanting fight

indicators.note: the shortened stomachs go round the island, enclosing it
almost the whole word, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: bellies are stomachs
Cos (Kos) is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Fat-bellied holidaymakers touring a Greek island are spoiling for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose means aggressive and eager to fight, so it describes someone wanting a fight.

clue.text: Man with gloves on is perhaps to wash up

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A man in rubber gloves is likely about to do the dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The gloves suggest washing-up gloves, but they are boxing gloves; 'perhaps' scrambles TO WASH UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, and boxers fight with gloves on.

clue.text: In old actor there's grand set of characters

indicators.note: grand goes inside the pair for old actor

parts.note: a ham is an overacting actor
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: An old ham actor gives a grand performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is an ancient Celtic alphabet, a set of written characters cut on stones.

clue.text: One boasting of getting man? Older woman needs doctor for head

indicators.note: the doctor replaces the first letter, the head, of the older woman

parts.note: an auntie is an older woman, often a familiar term
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: An elderly lady boasts of landing a husband, though she needs a doctor to sort her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs' is a link. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police are said always to 'get their man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie belongs to the Canadian police force whose motto boasts that it always gets its man.

clue.text: Bag with the other things I stuffed in appearing in order

indicators.note: the stuffed abbreviation sits inside the word for order

parts.note: rule means order, as in law and order

indicators.note: I is pushed into the abbreviation for the other things

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the other things

explanation.surface: A bag holds various odds and ends, everything kept neatly in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticule is a small woman's handbag, historically a drawstring pouch.

clue.text: Shot, but heal completely

definitions.meaning: a film or photographic shot taken from very near
a wound that knits together fully

explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a camera shot taken near the subject; close up also means a wound sealing over.

clue.text: King once in Britain, hiding in flipping oak

indicators.note: the country's abbreviation tucks itself inside the turned tree

parts.note: an oak is a tree
GB is Great Britain

explanation.surface: An old king hid in an oak tree, as the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The story of a king hiding in an oak belongs to Charles II, which makes 'King once' tempting to read that way; Egbert was a ninth-century king of Wessex.
explanation.definitionFit: Egbert was a ninth-century king of Wessex, so he was a king in former times.

clue.text: Foreign dish concocted with rum and pate

indicators.note: concocted means mixed up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An exotic recipe combining rum with pâté.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is a Japanese dish of battered, deep-fried fish or vegetables, a foreign dish to British eyes.

clue.text: Elementary thing like this people accept

indicators.note: the people take in, enclose, the word for like this

parts.note: men means people
so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: People accept something basic in just this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A meson is a subatomic particle, an elementary particle in physics.

clue.text: Showing great well-being, like some worms

definitions.meaning: giving off light, as glow-worms do

explanation.definitionFit: Glowing means radiant with health, and glow-worms give off light.

clue.text: Style senior officer's taken with corps

parts.note: Gen is the abbreviation for general
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A general adopts a style along with his regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a type or style of art, music or writing.

clue.text: Instruct postman at tight letter box to try something new

definitions.text: Instruct postman at tight letter box
definitions.meaning: an order to a postman to force mail through a stiff letter flap
to go beyond the usual limits

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to extend the limits of what is possible, attempting something innovative.

clue.text: Got cuddly toy as prize, as usual

parts.note: won means got, especially as a prize
ted is short for teddy, a cuddly toy bear

explanation.surface: Someone won a teddy bear at the fair, just as they always do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As prize' and 'as' are link words; the definition is usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonted means customary or habitual, an old-fashioned synonym of usual.

clue.text: Arrange introduction to old wife?

definitions.meaning: help two people meet, so act as matchmaker
an archaic word for a spouse, a helpmate

explanation.definitionFit: Helpmeet is an archaic word for a wife or helpful partner, from the King James Bible.
